entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Artabanus IV of Parthia, also known as Ardavan IV, was the last monarch of the Parthian Empire, ruling from approximately 213 to 224 CE. His reign was marked by the decline of the Parthian Empire and the rise of the Sassanian Empire.

Born to Vologases V in the late 2nd century CE, Artabanus IV ascended to the throne following his father's death in 208. His reign was characterized by internal conflicts, economic decline, and a series of military defeats.

The Parthian Empire, once a major power in the ancient world, began to crumble under Artabanus IV's leadership. The Sassanian Empire, led by Shapur I, eventually conquered the Parthian Empire in 224 CE, marking the end of the Parthian Empire's independence.

Artabanus IV's legacy is often overshadowed by his predecessors, but his reign served as a crucial turning point in the history of the ancient Near East. His failure to stem the decline of the Parthian Empire paved the way for the rise of new powers in the region.

The 'Artabanus IV' quote I found in the writings of the Roman historian Eusebius of Caesarea captures the essence of his reign: 'Artabanus IV, the last of the Parthians, who, though he had a large army, was unable to defend his country.'
